explanation.text: The 2019 revision of the International System of Units (SI) retained the mole as an SI base unit for amount of substance.
The SI Brochure (2018), published by the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures (BIPM), explicitly lists the mole among the seven base units under the updated definitions.
The definition of the mole was revised in 2019 to be based on a fixed value of the Avogadro constant, confirming its continued status as an SI base unit.
A peer-reviewed article authored by metrology experts from BIPM, NIST, PTB, and other national institutes confirms that the mole is defined under the 2019 SI revision effective from 20 May 2019.
The 2019 definition states that the mole, symbol mol, is the SI unit of amount of substance.
The revision of the mole's definition under the 2019 SI did not remove its status as a base unit but instead redefined it in terms of a fixed number of elementary entities.
